subject: maths
title: 2-D and 3-D Shapes: Sides, Symmetry, Faces, Edges and Vertices
seo_title: Year 2 2-D and 3-D Shapes Worksheets: Sides, Symmetry and Faces (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Identify and describe the properties of 2-D shapes, including the number of sides and line symmetry in a vertical line; identify and describe the properties of 3-D shapes, including the number of edges, vertices and faces; identify 2-D shapes on the surface of 3-D shapes; compare and sort common 2-D and 3-D shapes and everyday objects.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on 2-D and 3-D shapes: count sides and vertices, find a vertical line of symmetry, count the faces, edges and vertices of cubes, cuboids and pyramids, spot 2-D shapes on 3-D shapes and sort everyday objects. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Count the sides to name a 2-D shape. Count faces, edges and vertices to describe a 3-D shape.
key_sub: A shape keeps its name when it is turned. A line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that match exactly. Remember the faces you cannot see.
body_html:
2-D shapes

A 2-D shape is flat. Count its sides to find its name. A vertex is a corner. Two or more corners are called vertices.

ShapeSidesVertices
Circle1 curved side0
Triangle33
Square4 (all the same length)4
Rectangle4 (2 long, 2 short)4
Pentagon55
Hexagon66
Octagon88

Turning a shape does not change its name. The sides do not have to be the same length.

Example 1

A shape has 5 straight sides. Two sides are longer than the others. What is it?

Count the sides: 5. The lengths do not matter.

Answer: a pentagon

Line of symmetry

Fold a shape on a line. If the two halves match exactly, the line is a line of symmetry. In Year 2 we look for a line going straight down the middle (a vertical line).

Example 2

Is a line straight down the middle of a rectangle a line of symmetry?

Fold the rectangle in half from left to right. The two halves are the same size and shape.

Answer: yes

3-D shapes

A 3-D shape is solid, like a box or a ball. A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner. Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

ShapeFacesEdgesVerticesLike a…
Cube6 squares128dice
Cuboid6 rectangles128cereal box
Pyramid (square at the bottom)1 square, 4 triangles85Egyptian pyramid
Cylinder2 flat circles and a curved surface2 curved edges0tin of beans
Cone1 flat circle and a curved surface1 curved edge1 (the point)party hat
Spherea curved surface only00football

The flat faces of 3-D shapes are 2-D shapes. A cube has square faces. A cylinder has circle faces. A pyramid has triangle faces.

Example 3

How many faces does a cube have?

You can see 3 faces in a picture. There are 3 more at the back, on the other side and underneath. 3 + 3 = 6.

Answer: 6 faces

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a turned square a “diamond”Check the sides: 4 sides the same length and 4 square corners make a square
Counting only the faces you can seeRemember the faces at the back and underneath
Mixing up edges and verticesEdges are the lines where faces meet. Vertices are the corners
Thinking any line through the middle is a line of symmetryFold it in your head: both halves must match exactly
Using a 2-D name for a 3-D shapeA ball is a sphere, not a circle. A dice is a cube, not a square
Mixing up a cylinder and a coneA cylinder has 2 circle faces. A cone has 1 circle face and a point

faq.q: What 2-D and 3-D shapes should a Year 2 child know?
faq.a: 2-D: circle, triangle, square, rectangle, pentagon, hexagon and octagon. 3-D: cube, cuboid, pyramid, cylinder, cone and sphere.

faq.q: What is a vertical line of symmetry?
faq.a: It is a line straight down the middle of a shape. If you fold the shape on it, the two halves match exactly.

faq.q: How many faces, edges and vertices does a cube have?
faq.a: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A cuboid has the same numbers, but its faces are rectangles.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn shapes at home?
faq.a: Look for shapes around the house, such as a tin of beans (cylinder) or a cereal box (cuboid), and count the faces together. Fold paper shapes to find lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count each vertex as you go round, until you get back to the start: 8 vertices. Count the small corners too.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a circle have?
items.e: A circle has 1 curved side and no corners. So it has 0 vertices.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: A has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon. The other shapes have 5, 8 and 4 sides.

items.q: A shape has 4 sides. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It has 4 square corners. What is it?
items.e: 4 sides and 4 square corners, with 2 long sides and 2 short sides: a rectangle. A square has 4 sides the same length.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length, and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: A shape has 6 straight sides. What is it called?
items.e: 6 sides make a hexagon. 5 sides make a pentagon. 8 sides make an octagon.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count each vertex as you go round, until you get back to the start: 5 vertices.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 8 sides. It is an octagon.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices. It is a triangle.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 5 sides. It is a pentagon.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices. It is a triangle. A long, thin triangle is still a triangle.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 6 sides.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length, and 4 square corners. It is a square. It is only turned. “Diamond” is not its maths name.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 6 sides. It is a hexagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 5 sides. It is a pentagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.

items.q: Which shape is a square?
items.e: C has 4 sides that are the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square that is turned. The other shape with equal sides has no square corners, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It is flat and round, with no corners. It is a circle. A sphere is a 3-D shape, like a ball.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 6 sides. It is a hexagon.

items.q: Which dashed line is a line of symmetry?
items.e: B goes straight down the middle. The two halves match when you fold. A slanted line, a line across or a line that is not in the middle does not work here.
D goes straight down the middle. The two halves match when you fold. A slanted line, a line across or a line that is not in the middle does not work here.

items.q: Which dashed line is a line of symmetry?
items.e: Fold A on the dashed line: the two halves match exactly. In the others, the two sides do not match, or the line is not in the middle.

items.q: How many of the dashed lines are lines of symmetry?
items.e: Fold each shape in your head on the dashed line. Do the two halves match? All 4 match, so all 4 lines are lines of symmetry.

items.q: Which dashed line is NOT a line of symmetry?
items.e: Look at C. The line is not in the middle. One side is bigger than the other. The other lines cut the shapes into two halves that match.
Look at B. The line is in the middle, but the two sides are different shapes. They do not match when you fold. The other lines cut the shapes into two halves that match.

items.q: Which dashed line is a line of symmetry?
items.e: A goes straight down the middle. The two halves match when you fold. A slanted line, a line across or a line that is not in the middle does not work here.

items.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry going straight down the middle?
items.e: A is the same on the left and the right, so a line down the middle is a line of symmetry. F, L and J do not match.
Fold each shape in your head on the dashed line. Do the two halves match? 3 of them match, so 3 lines are lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many of the dashed lines are lines of symmetry?
items.e: Fold each shape in your head on the dashed line. Do the two halves match? Only 1 of them matches, so 1 line is a line of symmetry.

items.e: C goes straight down the middle. The two halves match when you fold. A slanted line, a line across or a line that is not in the middle does not work here.
Fold D on the dashed line: the two halves match exactly. In the others, the two sides do not match, or the line is not in the middle.
Fold D on the dashed line: the two halves match exactly. In the others, the two sides do not match, or the line is not in the middle.

items.q: How many of the dashed lines are lines of symmetry?
items.e: Fold each shape in your head on the dashed line. Do the two halves match? 3 of them match, so 3 lines are lines of symmetry.

items.q: Which dashed line is a line of symmetry?
items.e: Fold B on the dashed line: the two halves match exactly. In the others, the two sides do not match, or the line is not in the middle.

items.q: Which capital letter does NOT have a line of symmetry going straight down the middle?
items.e: T, U and M are the same on both sides of a line down the middle. S is not.

items.q: How many of the dashed lines are lines of symmetry?
items.e: Fold each shape in your head on the dashed line. Do the two halves match? 2 of them match, so 2 lines are lines of symmetry.
Fold C on the dashed line: the two halves match exactly. In the others, the two sides do not match, or the line is not in the middle.
Look at A. The line is in the middle, but the two sides are different shapes. They do not match when you fold. The other lines cut the shapes into two halves that match.

items.q: You fold a shape on a line. The two halves match exactly. What is the line called?
items.e: When the two halves match exactly, the fold line is a line of symmetry.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has a square at the bottom. Its triangle faces meet at a point at the top. It is a pyramid.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square at the bottom. Its triangle faces meet at a point at the top. It is a pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a pyramid.

items.q: A corner of a 3-D shape is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. An edge is where two faces meet. A face is a flat surface.

items.q: This pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many edges does it have?
items.e: This pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines are edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: This pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.
It has 1 flat circle face. Its curved surface comes to a point. It is a cone.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines are edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back and underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.
It has 1 flat circle face. Its curved surface comes to a point. It is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces, and they are not all squares. It is a cuboid.
It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface. It is a cylinder.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are all squares of the same size. It is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: This pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many faces does it have?
items.e: This pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back and underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are all squares of the same size. It is a cube.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces, and they are not all squares. It is a cuboid. It is standing on its end, but it is still a cuboid.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back and underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.
It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface. It is a cylinder. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.
It is round all over, like a ball. It is a sphere. A circle is a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: Noah dips a slanted face of a pyramid in paint. Then he presses it on paper. What shape does he print?
items.e: The slanted faces go up to the point. They are triangles. So it prints a triangle.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has a square face and triangle faces?
items.e: A pyramid can have a square at the bottom and triangles going up to the point. A cube has only squares. A cone has a circle.

items.q: Ava dips a face of a cube in paint. Then she presses it on paper. What shape does she print?
items.e: Every face of a cube is a square. So it prints a square.
A is a cylinder. Its 2 flat faces are circles. The others have squares, rectangles or triangles.
Each end of a cylinder is a flat circle. In a picture it looks like an oval, because we see it from the side.

items.q: Ethan dips the big flat face of a cereal box in paint. Then he presses it on paper. What shape does he print?
items.e: A cereal box is a cuboid. Its big face is a long rectangle, not a square. So it prints a rectangle.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 1 flat circle face and a point?
items.e: A cone has 1 circle face and its curved surface comes to a point. A pyramid has a point too, but its bottom is a square.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 2 flat circle faces?
items.e: A cylinder has a flat circle at each end: 2 circles. A cone has only 1 circle.

items.q: What shape are the faces of this cuboid?
items.e: The faces of this cuboid are rectangles. Each face has 4 sides and 4 square corners.

items.q: How many flat circle faces does a cylinder have?
items.e: A cylinder has 1 flat circle at the top and 1 at the bottom: 2 circles.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 6 square faces?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces and they are all squares. A cuboid has rectangle faces.

items.q: Ruby dips the end of a cylinder in paint. Then she presses it on paper. What shape does she print?
items.e: The end of a cylinder is a flat circle face. So it prints a circle. A print is always a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: A pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many triangle faces does it have?
items.e: There is 1 triangle on each side of the square. The square has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangles. 5 counts the square too.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has no flat faces at all?
items.e: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has a curved surface and no flat faces.
C is a pyramid. Its faces that meet at the top are triangles.

items.q: What shape are the faces that meet at the top of this pyramid?
items.e: The faces that meet at the point are triangles. Only the bottom face is a square.

items.q: What shape is the face at the bottom of this pyramid?
items.e: This pyramid stands on a square face. The faces going up to the point are triangles.

items.q: How many square faces does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces. You can see 3 in a picture. 3 more are at the back and underneath.

items.q: What shape are the faces of this cube?
items.e: All 6 faces of a cube are squares. A cube is a 3-D shape. Its faces are flat 2-D shapes.
The flat face at the bottom of a cone is a circle. From the side a cone looks like a triangle, but it has no triangle faces.

sets.title: Sort and compare shapes: word problems

items.q: Which object has 1 flat circle face and a point?
items.e: An ice-cream cone is a cone. It has 1 circle at the top and a point at the bottom.

items.q: A 3-D shape has 6 faces. They are all squares of the same size. What is it?
items.e: 6 square faces, all the same size: it is a cube. A cuboid has rectangle faces.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a cereal box?
items.e: A cereal box has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. It is a cuboid.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a tin of beans?
items.e: A tin has 2 flat circle ends and a curved side. It is a cylinder.

items.q: Harry has a rubber shaped like a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left and right. 3 is only the faces you can see at once. 12 is the edges and 8 is the vertices.

items.q: Which 2-D shape is the odd one out: triangle, square, circle, pentagon?
items.e: A circle has a curved side and no corners. The others have straight sides and vertices.

items.q: Poppy puts a sticker on every vertex of a cube. How many stickers does she use?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. 6 is the number of faces. 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Isla counts the square faces on a cube. Oliver counts the triangle faces on a pyramid. How many more faces does Isla count?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces. A pyramid has 4 triangle faces. 6 − 4 = 2 more. 10 adds them instead of finding the difference.

items.q: A 3-D shape has 5 faces. 4 faces are triangles and 1 is a square. What is it?
items.e: A pyramid with a square at the bottom has 1 square face and 4 triangle faces: 5 faces.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a dice?
items.e: A dice has 6 square faces, all the same size. It is a cube.

items.q: Leo sorts some 3-D shapes. Group 1: cube, cuboid, pyramid. Group 2: sphere, cylinder, cone. What do the shapes in group 2 have?
items.e: A sphere, a cylinder and a cone all have a curved surface. They can roll. The shapes in group 1 have only flat faces.

items.q: Grace makes a pyramid from straws. Each edge is one straw. The pyramid has a square at the bottom. How many straws does she need?
items.e: The pyramid has 8 edges: 4 round the square and 4 going up to the top. So she needs 8 straws. 5 is the number of vertices.

items.q: Jack has 2 dice. How many faces do the 2 dice have altogether?
items.e: A dice is a cube with 6 faces. 6 + 6 = 12. 16 counts the vertices (8 + 8).

items.q: What 3-D shape is a football?
items.e: A football is round all over. It is a sphere. A circle is flat.

items.q: Charlie draws 2 triangles and 1 square. How many sides is that altogether?
items.e: Each triangle has 3 sides and a square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10. 7 forgets one triangle.

items.q: A STOP road sign is an octagon. How many sides does it have?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides and 8 vertices.

items.q: Which of these can roll, and can also stand in a tall stack?
items.e: A tin is a cylinder. It rolls on its curved side and stacks on its flat circle faces. A football rolls but will not stack.

items.q: Which of these can roll?
items.e: A ball is a sphere. It has a curved surface, so it can roll. The others have only flat faces.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a party hat?
items.e: A party hat has a circle at the bottom and a point at the top. It is a cone.

items.q: Which 3-D shape is the odd one out: cube, cuboid, sphere, pyramid?
items.e: The sphere has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices. The other shapes all have flat faces, edges and vertices.
